claim: Every new attribute is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. As a result, generated code compiled for netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework gets no `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage` at all. `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists on both (.NET Framework 4.0+ and .NET Standard 2.0) and can be applied to classes, so the exclusion is not needed for compilation. It breaks the 'All generated code is decorated' criterion for a very common class of consumers (netstandard2.0 libraries, net472 apps). The README states the wrong availability claim as fact.
